# @agimon-ai/doompi-web

Package-owned guidance for the DoomPi Web cockpit.

## Start here

- [README](./README.md): installation, command options, runtime behavior, extensions, and security summary.
- [Getting started](./docs/getting-started.md): setup, synchronization, session discovery, and local development.
- [Architecture](./docs/architecture.md): terminal, browser, and client-neutral headless ownership boundaries.
- [Web plugins](./docs/plugins.md): `doompiWeb.client`, `webPlugin`, and browser UI contributions.
- [Package APIs](./docs/package-apis.md): canonical `doompiServer` facets, scopes, and request context.
- [Web bundling and serving](./docs/bundle.md): browser assets, authenticated proxying, and the separate server descriptor.
- [Remote security](./docs/security.md): pairing, device cookies, passkeys, step-up actions, sealing, signed assets, and containment limits.

## Facts to preserve

- DoomPi Web owns presentation delivery only. It does not own sessions, APIs, channels, authorization, replay, or server facets.
- Browser plugins declare only `doompiWeb.client`; host-side channels and APIs register through `doompiServer` in the client-neutral headless process.
- Browser HTTP and the binary Pi 0.85 WebSocket use the authenticated headless boundary at `/api/pi`; `/api/session` and internal `/frame` are retired.
- The headless process loads only the admitted generation-pinned `server.bundle.json`, owns session and native Team child lifecycle, and keeps browser disconnects independent from session lifetime.
- DoomPi Web may serve or proxy browser assets and API traffic, but it does not interpret protocol frames or receive the headless credential in browser code.
- The PWA has a package-owned service worker that verifies signed host and plugin assets before caching them. Optional closed-app Web Push is generic, zero-TTL, in-memory delivery, not a durable queue.
- Remote access is not a sandbox. Pairing requires host approval, remote sockets and API bodies use sealed channels, and a paired device can drive an agent with shell access. Loopback origin and host checks do not defend against hostile local programs.
- Bundle signatures provide delivery integrity only after the signer key and the initial executable bootstrap are trusted separately. A tunnel provider can observe bootstrap traffic, timing, sizes, and connection metadata.
- Dev proxy targets forward `/devproxy/<name>/` to a local dev server on the cockpit's own origin and listener, passing the path through unchanged. The proxied app must be configured with a matching base path, exactly as behind nginx, or its assets escape the prefix; stripping the prefix instead would loop against its own base redirect. Registering a target is loopback-only; using one is open to any paired device. The upstream is a port plus one of two hard-coded loopback literals, `127.0.0.1` or `::1`, never a resolved hostname. Proxied traffic is neither sealed nor signature-checked.
